description: On hearing of emptiness, great joy arising again and again, eyes filling with tears and body hair standing on end — the sign of one who has the seed of awakening and is a vessel for the teaching.
Terror at the thought 'I am not, I will not be, nothing is mine' — the reaction of the childish to the teaching of definite goodness, which for the wise ends fear.
When neither an entity nor its non-existence remains before the mind, having no other recourse the mind is pacified without object.
When the yogin, analysing with correct wisdom, sees no dharma arisen in the three times, he enters non-conceptual wisdom, pacifying all elaboration, and penetrates emptiness.
The mind placed, re-placed, stabilized, closely placed, tamed, pacified, fully pacified, made one-pointed and brought into equipoise on its object.
Laziness, forgetting the object, laxity and excitement, non-application and over-application — the faults met in concentration.

On the first ground the bodhisattva gains twelve sets of a hundred qualities — seeing a hundred Buddhas, receiving their blessing, living a hundred aeons, entering a hundred concentrations, shaking and illuminating a hundred world-systems, ripening a hundred beings, going to a hundred Buddha-fields, opening a hundred doors of Dharma and displaying a hundred bodies each with a hundred attendants — multiplied on the higher grounds.
Suffering brings the loss of pride, compassion for those in saṃsāra, shrinking from evil and longing for the Victor.
